# Precedent: Editorial Composition and Typography

Surfaces where typography and editorial structure carry hierarchy and identity. Observed
2026-09-24; IDs refer to `research/observations/`.

---

### The Guardian — pillar colors and serif headlines
`GU3 GU4` · https://www.theguardian.com/international · rendered
- **What works:** heavy serif headlines; each section pillar has its own color used for navigation and
  kicker labels; a red "Live" kicker for live coverage.
- **Lesson:** a typographic system plus a color system tied to the information architecture.

### Wikipedia — text-first structure
`WPd1 WPm2` · https://en.wikipedia.org/ · rendered
- **What works:** serif title, dense but comfortable body, hatnotes subordinated in a tinted box.

### Our World in Data — question-led titles
`OW1 OW2` · https://ourworldindata.org/co2-emissions · rendered
- **What works:** centered serif title with the questions the page answers; citation and reuse tools
  beside the byline.
- **Lesson:** content-first credibility is typographic and structural.

### The Pudding — crafted voice
`PU1 PU2 PU3` · https://pudding.cool/ · rendered
- **What works:** hand-lettered wordmark, hand-drawn navigation, issue numbers and dates on each story.

### Stripe — two-tone headline
`SR1` · https://stripe.com/ · rendered
- **What works:** one paragraph with the first phrase dark and the rest grey: hierarchy without a subhead.

### Patagonia — serif statement
`PA1` · https://www.patagonia.com/home/ · rendered
- **What works:** a large serif statement on black carries a values message before products.

### Claude — serif as identity for a focused page
`CL2` · https://claude.ai/login · rendered
- **What works:** a serif display line makes a centered sign-in recognizable.

### Apple — scale as hierarchy
`AP2` · https://www.apple.com/iphone/ · rendered
- **What works:** a very large product-name heading followed by a model navigator.

### MDN — code in titles
`MD4` · https://developer.mozilla.org/ · rendered
- **What works:** the property name in code style inside the title marks what kind of thing the page is.

### Wise — condensed uppercase display
`W4` · https://wise.com/ · rendered
- **What works:** heavy condensed uppercase display type as brand voice over a plain form.

### Codecademy — type as editor
`CC2` · https://www.codecademy.com/ · rendered
- **What works:** headline blocks, slash, and cursor make type behave like code.

---

## Summary rules

1. Choose type by role (display, UI, body, data) and let display carry the voice.
2. Tie color systems to information architecture where possible (sections, states).
3. Use one-paragraph hierarchy (two tones, weight) before adding eyebrow labels and subheads.
4. Content-first pages earn credibility through structure: bylines, dates, citations, versions.
